slides.texte_overlay:
Skills that make you the friend
everyone calls in a crisis
Basic first aid. A weekend course teaches you CPR, how to stop bleeding and what to do when someone faints. It's the one skill you hope never to use and will never regret having.
Staying calm on the phone. When a friend calls panicking, lower your voice and slow down. "Okay, tell me exactly what happened." Your calm becomes their calm within seconds.
Knowing how to change a tyre and jump a car. Friends stuck on the side of the road at night will remember forever the guy who showed up and fixed it in twenty minutes.
Listening without fixing straight away. Sometimes a friend in crisis just needs to talk. Ask "Do you want advice or do you just need me to listen?" and respect the answer.
Before: no idea what to say when things went wrong. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, a calmer head and a wider view to help friends think clearly.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: no idea what to say when things went wrong. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A calmer head to help friends.

slides.texte_overlay: Keeping some money aside. A small emergency fund means you can cover a train ticket, a night in a hotel or a meal for a friend who's had the worst week of their life.
Following up after the storm. A message a week later, "How are you holding up?" Most people disappear once the crisis is over. Real friends check in when it's quiet again.
